why_was_i_in_the_buffer.door_1: The transporter log. Accessible from any engineering console. The entry is disguised as routine maintenance but a careful read — or asking Ryder to pull the raw timestamps — reveals the command authorization and the 11-minute gap before evacuation.
why_was_i_in_the_buffer.door_1_cost: Time and attention. Ryder would help if asked.
why_was_i_in_the_buffer.door_2: Ask Captain Solano directly. She is reachable if comms are restored — or her personal logs in her ready room may hold something. Cost: breaking into the captain's quarters/ready room, which the crew will notice and have opinions about.
why_was_i_in_the_buffer.door_3: The player's own fragmented memories. Pursuing them — meditation, sensory triggers, places on the ship associated with the missing 40 minutes — may recover pieces. Cost: each recovered memory comes with a flash of the lattice's perspective, which is disorienting and increasingly alien.

what_is_the_resonance.door_1: Run a deep-spectrum harmonic analysis on the planetary lattice from the science console. Okafor can help but has not thought of it. Cost: requires diverting sensor power from monitoring the crew's condition.
what_is_the_resonance.door_2: The player character's own anomalous perceptions. As the lattice fragments surface, they begin to sense things about the resonance that instruments cannot measure. Cost: each episode of alien perception is involuntary and alarming.
what_is_the_resonance.door_3: Go to the planet. The lattice is loudest at its source. A shuttlecraft is gone but the transporter could beam someone to the surface — if someone can be spared from keeping the ship running. Cost: extreme exposure to the resonance, and the crew is already short-handed.

why_are_the_women_affected_differently.door_1: Vasari's medical data, cross-referenced with the sensor readings. The correlation between resonance frequency shifts and specific neurochemical changes is there in the data — but it requires someone to look at both datasets together.
why_are_the_women_affected_differently.door_2: The crew themselves. Their experiences of the disinhibition are not uniform — some are more affected than others, and the pattern maps to something. Interviewing them would reveal it. Cost: the interviews are going to be very frank, because the crew's filters are dissolving.
why_are_the_women_affected_differently.door_3: The player character is the control group. They were stored during the transition. Vasari scanning them against baseline and against the affected crew would show the intermediate state — if the player consents to be scanned and the results are interpreted correctly.

what_happened_to_solano.door_1: Her ready room logs. She kept personal audio logs. They are behind her command lockout but Chandrasekaran could bypass it with engineering access — if she is willing.
what_happened_to_solano.door_2: The bridge sensor recordings from the evacuation. Automated. They show the bridge during the 40-minute window. Cost: someone has to think to look at them.
what_happened_to_solano.door_3: Ask the crew what they saw. Several bridge crew are still aboard. They were busy during the evacuation but someone may have noticed Solano doing something unusual. Cost: the crew is protective of their captain and may not cooperate easily.
